text.content:
Source: C. Hettlestad, “Healers,” The Dragon #3 (October 1976), p.22-23, in “A Plethora of Obscure Sub-Classes”; reprinted in The Best of Dragon vol. II, p.12-13. The rules and spells follow the reprint; the level table, which the reprint leaves out, is from The Dragon #3. Restated in plain words; the numbers follow the article.

In The Dragon #3 the editor put a note in front of these sub-classes. The authors of the game asked him to stress that none of them are official. He urges caution before letting odd sub-classes into a campaign, since they often make the DM's job harder and are often too strong for player characters, and he says that many of them are meant as non-player characters.

The healer exists to patch up other characters quickly in big campaign games. Think of a magic-user and a cleric with a little fighter mixed in. Healers have their own spell list (though most of the spells are also found in other lists). A healer can never decide to switch to another class.

Requirements

  • Intelligence, wisdom and dexterity of 15 or more each.
  • Lawful or neutral. There are no chaotic healers: a healer forced out of lawful or neutral becomes an ordinary fighter.
  • Human, dwarf, halfling, half-elf or elf. A dwarf can go no higher than 10th level (Medic); a halfling, half-elf or elf no higher than 14th.

Armor, weapons and magic items

No armor and no shield. A healer can use, and be affected by, any weapon and any magic item. The various magical books, librams and tomes found in adventures never help a healer; they can only do harm.

Powers gained by level

  • 4th: senses molds, slimes and the like within 40 feet.
  • 8th: can identify the general type of a potion.
  • 12th: can read magic-user and cleric scrolls.
  • 16th: can use four 1st level magic-user spells, on top of the healer spells.
  • 20th: can use four 2nd level magic-user spells, on top of the healer spells.

Level table (The Dragon #3)

Hit dice are 8-sided. The columns 1 to 7 give the healer spells per day of each spell level.

The healer has 42 spells, six at each of seven spell levels. All are in the Healer Spells compendium. Where the article says a spell is the “same as” a magic-user or cleric spell, the entry carries that spell's text. The healer's own spells are restated from the reprint, which gives only a short description of each: range, duration and other details it leaves out are for the DM.

The list below is the reprint's (The Best of Dragon vol. II).

1st level

Detect Magic, Detect Evil, Detect Poison, Detect Disease, Detect Invisibility, Detect Phase.

2nd level

Neutralize Poison, Cure Disease, Purify Food & Drink, Slow, Haste, Invisibility.

3rd level

Speak With Dead, Cure Serious Wounds, Cure Blindness, ESP, Animate Dead, Strength.

4th level

Stone To Flesh, Mind Blank, Energy, Cure Lycanthropy, Awaken, Fly.

5th level

Raise Dead, Cure Insanity, Cure Paralysis, Longevity, Teleport, Size Control.

6th level

Improved Cure Serious Wounds, Clone, Water Breathing, Speak With Plants, Speak With Animals, Speak With Monsters.

7th level

Sterilize, Neutralize Gas, Blade Barrier, Remove Curse, Remove Charm, Cure Deafness.

How The Dragon #3 differs

  • 3rd level: raise dead (“same as clerical spell”) in place of speak with dead.
  • 5th level: raise dead fully (“same as clerical spell of same name”) in place of raise dead.
  • Names: detect invisible (1st), purify food & water (2nd), stone-flesh and wake spell (4th), talks to plants in the list and talk to plants in the description (6th).
  • Cure blindness is the healer's own spell: it cures blindness from any cause, curses included.
  • Talk to plants lets the caster talk to any plant. Speak with animals lets the caster speak to any animal, though the animal decides whether to answer.
  • Sterilize cleans any room of any infection, mold, slime or nasty creatures of up to 5 hit dice. Neutralize gas neutralizes poison gas, tear gas or any other gas. Remove charm removes a charm once cast on the charmed character, range 3”.
  • Wake spell wakes anyone put to sleep by “various means” (the reprint: any means). Detect disease has a range of “30” with no unit (the reprint: 30”).
  • Improved cure serious wounds is printed “8 to 24 pts.” (the reprint: 8-28, which matches 4d6 plus one per die).

What the module does

  • Adds the class Healer (The Dragon #3) with its own spell list, Healer, and the article's spells per day and hit dice.
  • From 16th level the healer also gets four 1st level magic-user spell slots, and from 20th four 2nd level ones, on the Spells tab.
  • The Record tab shows notes, which never block anything: an intelligence, wisdom or dexterity below 15, a race or level not allowed, a chaotic alignment, more than one class, and armor worn.

Choices made here

  • Experience: the cleric's table by default. The world setting Healer experience table switches to the article's own (5,000 at 2nd level to 1,900,000 at 25th).
  • Hit dice: the table shows “10+1” to “10+15” after 10th level. The module reads that as 10 dice, then +1 hit point a level.
  • Not in the article: the cleric's attack table and saving throws, the cleric's proficiency slots and −3 when not proficient, no bonus spells for wisdom, no turning undead.
  • A healer with more than one class is noted, since a healer can never switch class.
  • Rules and spells: the reprint's, with the differences in The Dragon #3 on the Spells page. The level table and experience are from The Dragon #3, since the reprint leaves them out.
